claims.statement: Determinism: the execution relation for and.b32 is deterministic for any well-formed state and well-typed instruction, because the value written is fully determined by the values read (a pure bitwise-and of fixed 32-bit values, no arithmetic, no truncation, no rounding) and the guard evaluation is a deterministic function of the predicate register value. Determinism is NOT explicitly stated in the bundle (architecture assumption A-3 records the same absence); this is a derived interpretation stated as proof obligation PRF-1.

Execution-semantics representation design (architecture D-25): the future execution semantics for and.b32 is designed to be represented as an execution relation between (state, instruction) and state, not merely as a function, so that determinism and frame/locality obligations are non-vacuous.

Execution-result representation design (architecture D-8): an instruction-local outcome has at least two cases: executed (with destination update) and guard-false (no state change, per derived interpretation PTX-AND-SEM2-063); no error constructor is proposed because no explicit exceptional behavior for the bounded base and.b32 is evidenced.

Bitwise-and semantics: when and.b32 executes with register sources, the value written to the destination register d equals the bitwise-and of the values read from sources a and b, computed over the 32-bit untyped .b32 value domain; when b is a constant immediate, the AND is computed between the value of a and the immediate value. This is derived from 'd = a & b;' (AND_SEMANTICS), 'Bitwise AND.' (AND_TARGET_SECTION), 'Compute the bit-wise and operation for the bits in a and b.' (AND_DESCRIPTION), and the .b32 'Bits (untyped)' 32-bit type (CTX-04, CTX-03). The exact formal statement (representation of bitwise-and over the 32-bit bit-value domain) is a semantic-phase matter (OQ-8; claim PTX-AND-SEM2-068).

Guard-true behavior: when the complete guard expression evaluates true (including the no-guard case), the instruction executes: the pre-instruction values of source operands a and b are read (or the immediate value of b is used), and the destination register d is updated with the bitwise-and of those values. This is consistent with the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (CTX-08).

No explicit error, trap, or exceptional-behavior clause for and (or and.b32) was found in the bundle. The absence is not asserted as a positive source fact; no error, trap, or exceptional behavior is invented. Whether the absence means no such behaviors exist is unresolved.

State read: the instruction reads source operands a and b. When they are registers, their current (pre-instruction) values are read from the value-register file; when b is a constant immediate (evidenced for the .b32 form), its value is the immediate constant. The description 'Compute the bit-wise and operation for the bits in a and b.' (AND_DESCRIPTION) and the Semantics 'd = a & b;' (AND_SEMANTICS) require these reads. Whether a may be a constant immediate is an open question (PTX-AND-SEM2-061).

State write: when the instruction executes with a real destination register, the destination register d is updated with the bitwise-and of the values read from sources a and b. The source states no other register write for the bounded base and.b32 form.

Aliasing/read-before-write: because the semantics is a bitwise-and (d = a & b;), the values of a and b are read before the destination update. No same-register example appears in the and section itself; the sibling or example 'or.b32 mask mask,0x00010001' (recorded in the architecture SF-A10, not in this bundle) uses the same name for destination and first source but belongs to the sibling instruction or and is not direct and.b32 evidence.

Section 9.7.13.2 'Control Flow Instructions: @' (HTML lines 21826-21854) defines the general predication form: Syntax '@{!}p instruction;' with Description 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' (CTX-08). This is the explicit official false-guard no-op clause that the mov.b32 Gate B lesson requires; by the general predicability rule (CTX-07) it is the applicable evidence for predicated instructions including and.b32.

Derivation chain for and.b32 guard behavior: (1) 'All PTX instructions may be predicated' (CTX-07); (2) 'All instructions have an optional guard predicate ... prefix an instruction with @{!}p' (CTX-02); (3) the general predication form's explicit rule 'Execute an instruction or instruction block for threads that have the guard predicate True. Threads with a False guard predicate do nothing.' and its Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (CTX-08); therefore the bounded base and.b32, when predicated, executes iff the complete guard expression is true, and does nothing (no state change) when the complete guard expression is false. This derived consequence consolidates the chain behind PTX-AND-SEM2-063.

Guard representation and evaluation: an optional guard prefix @{!}p (p a predicate register variable, optionally negated) appears to the left of the instruction; without a guard the instruction is executed unconditionally; with @p the complete guard expression is the value of p; with @!p the complete guard expression is the negation of the value of p.

Execution condition: the instruction executes if and only if the complete guard expression evaluates true. This is grounded in the explicit general-predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (CTX-08) together with the section 9.3 wording 'an optional guard predicate which controls conditional execution of the instruction' and 'Instructions without a guard predicate are executed unconditionally' (CTX-02).

This is consistent with the general predication Semantics 'If {!}p then instruction' (CTX-08).

State read: when a guard is present, the value of the predicate register referenced by the guard is read to evaluate the complete guard expression. CTX-02 establishes the guard mechanism and the @{!}p prefix with p a predicate variable; the general predication form of section 9.7.13.2 executes for threads whose guard predicate is True (CTX-08).
Static precondition PRE-5: if a guard is present, it refers to a predicate register variable of type .pred in the register state space, optionally negated.
